Sprites, fonts, sounds and UI art are read while the page runs, straight from the decomp projects (pret/pokeemerald and rh-hideout/pokeemerald-expansion) at the commits this page was built against. The page uses the first source that answers: the repo's vendor/ submodules, then a decomp this folder sits inside, then GitHub. It has to be served over http (python3 -m http.server 8000): opened as a file:// path, the browser won't let it read pixels back out of the art.
About this viewer
Cartridge Replay plays a Pokémon Showdown battle back as a Pokémon Emerald battle. Every battle is drawn with the game's own sprites, fonts, healthboxes and textbox, in the cartridge's 240×160 layout: the foe's box top-left and its Pokémon top-right, yours bottom-left and your box bottom-right.

What it plays: singles and doubles from every generation, including Mega Evolution, Z-Moves, Dynamax and Terastallization. Triples, free-for-all and multi battles are refused with a message. All 934 moves Showdown and pokeemerald-expansion share have their animation, ported line for line from the decomp. Gen 1–3 battles use Emerald's own scripts, and later generations use the expansion's. Send-outs, recalls, faints, stat changes, weather, held items and status conditions play the decomp's own scenes, with its sound effects and cries.

Where it isn't the cartridge: Showdown's log is the only input, so anything the log doesn't say takes the game's default. A few additions are the page's own, not the game's: the crit, miss, flinch and protect chips; the attack pose; the damage numbers; the foe's HP percentage; the turn tag; the score; and the battle log beside the screen. Emerald picks the terrain from where the battle happens. Here it's random unless you choose one in the settings menu (the gear), where you can also shorten or turn off the animations that come round every turn.

Controls: click the battle or press Space/K to play and pause; Left/Right step a turn; Home/End jump to the start or the end. Type a turn number into the bar to go straight there, and use the switch button to watch from the other player's side.

Loading a battle: Fetch takes a replay link or ID from replay.pokemonshowdown.com. If the browser blocks the request, or the battle was never uploaded, open Paste log and paste the raw log or the replay's .json.
Test bench (moves, statuses, weather, effects)
Sets up a throwaway two-Pokémon battle and fires individual pieces on it. Moves and statuses run through the same battle-anim engine the replay uses; the effect buttons call the same functions the parser hooks up.
